biography.plain_text: Jack Crawford Taylor was the American founder of Enterprise Rent-A-Car. A former Navy fighter pilot and Cadillac salesman based in St. Louis, he mortgaged his home to invest in a leasing partnership with his employer. He built the company into an international business that remained principally owned by his family.

long_biography.plain_text:
The replacement-car market gave Jack Taylor's Enterprise business a route beyond long-term leasing. He entrusted its early rental operation to assistant Don Holtzman, who sought customers away from airports and cultivated demand from insurance adjusters. Taylor continued developing this neighbourhood network after Holtzman left, supplying drivers whose own vehicles had been damaged or stolen.

His philanthropy also used a matching approach: a challenge gift encouraged others to contribute. In 2000 he committed $40 million to establish the St. Louis Symphony Endowment Trust when the orchestra faced financial collapse. The gift helped attract wider support and gave the orchestra a lasting financial reserve. Taylor continued supporting its endowment and programmes until his death.
